claims.text: Applying a nanoscale self-lubricating coating to CoCrFeNi will enable formation of a stable, low-shear transfer layer during sliding.
The transfer layer will maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The transfer layer will reduce wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating contains nanoscale lubricious phases.
Sliding causes the nanoscale lubricious phases to form a continuous, low-shear transfer layer at the contact interface.
During sliding, the coating releases or rearranges nanoscale lubricious particulates.
The released or rearranged particulates reduce interfacial shear resistance.
The particulates promote formation of an adherent transfer film.
The transfer film minimizes metal-to-metal contact and wear.
At lower temperatures, the coating maintains low friction.
At higher temperatures up to 800 °C, the transfer layer remains sufficiently stable to maintain beneficial low friction despite oxidation challenges.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeNi, coated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction throughout the tested range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeNi, coated CoCrFeNi will have reduced wear rates throughout the tested range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits higher friction and wear variability than the proposed coated material across the tested temperature range.
The intervention is effective only when the environment does not cause rapid oxidation or degradation of the lubricious phase.
Coating performance may become unstable above 800 °C.
Coating performance may not extend to extreme loads outside the tested conditions.
